title: Traffic-aware zone reservation and graceful degradation for dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a traffic-aware zone reservation policy and coordinated graceful degradation for regional dedicated fleets. Goal: provide per-customer throughput guarantees while minimizing cross-zone data egress and avoiding large-scale cascading evictions during AZ pressure. This ticket scopes the API surface, scheduler changes, autoscaling control loops, and the rollout strategy for selected customers in us-west and eu-central.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler honors per-fleet zone reservation buckets and refuses placement that violates customer residency tags
Autoscaler supports throughput-based scaling targets (tokens/sec) and a soft-buffer headroom setting per-fleet
Graceful degradation policy triggers prioritized backfills and prefix-KV cache preservation without violating residency constraints
E2E tests simulate AZ outage and show <5% request error rate increase for 'guaranteed' customers and controlled latency tail increase
Monitoring dashboards surface reserved vs. used capacity, failover events, and cross-zone egress in real time
design_notes: Use a dual-reservation model: 'hard' capacity reserved for guaranteed throughput; 'soft' buffer capacity used opportunistically with preemptible label
Represent residency constraints as immutable scheduling tags (region:k, data_region:k) attached to fleet and node resources
Admission control evaluates a weighted score: locality match (40%), reservation headroom (35%), cache affinity (25%)
During AZ pressure, prefer intra-region soft-evictions before cross-region migrations; apply staged fallback: local soft-buffer -> sibling-AZ warm-borrow -> regional cold-standby
Autoscaling loop operates on a throughput signal (rps and token consumption) with smoothing window and scale-in delay to avoid oscillation
engineering_notes: Scheduler patch: add ReservationBucket API and extend placement engine to evaluate reservation headroom
Autoscaler changes: new metric collector to emit per-fleet token/sec and 95th-percentile request size for capacity calculations
KV cache affinity: attach cache-key prefix fingerprint to pods; prefer placements that preserve >70% cache hit retention
Failover choreography: implement orchestrator handle that performs graceful redirection and marks nodes as 'draining-preserve-kv' to sustain streaming sessions
Storage/residency enforcement: admission rejects placement on nodes whose data_region tag conflicts with fleet residency tag; migration requires explicit cross-region approval in console
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Integration tests and synthetic traffic experiments on staging cluster (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Canary with 3 low-risk customers in us-west (one-week canary), monitor reserved vs used metrics
Phase 2: Expand to 10 customers and enable warm-borrow behavior across AZs (two weeks)
Phase 3: Enable for EU region and run cross-region residency enforcement smoke tests
Phase 4: GA and documentation update with configuration reference and cost-awareness guidance
test_plan: Unit tests for ReservationBucket evaluation and admission control
Integration test: deploy fleet with hard+soft buckets, push burst load and verify admissions and preemptions
Chaos test: simulate AZ fail 50% capacity and assert graceful degradation thresholds
Performance regression: ensure scheduler decision latency remains <50ms p95
Security: verify residency tags cannot be overridden by customer API
risks: Over-reserving capacity reduces overall platform utilization and increases cost; need conservative defaults
Incorrect cache-affinity scoring could cause large cold-start penalties after placement changes
Complex admission logic might increase scheduler latency under heavy churn
Customers may request cross-region placement for throughput reasons, conflicting with residency policies
mitigations: Expose soft-buffer size per plan and default to small headroom for P1 customers; run cost model to recommend settings
Shadow-roll cache-affinity scoring in staging to tune thresholds before enforcing
Benchmark scheduler changes under synthetic churn and add in-memory caches for scoring results
Add console approval flow and an auditable operator action for explicit cross-region migrations
